segments.title: A shared face
segments.caption: Predict the sign of the right face contribution to cell i. Then describe the same face from the neighboring cell.

segments.title: The global budget
segments.caption: Sum the three updates. Identify precisely which terms cancel and which boundary terms survive.

segments.title: Pressure-driven velocity
segments.caption: Integrate the reduced momentum equation twice. Explain the no-slip boundary data and the units of q.

segments.title: A transported packet
segments.caption: Compare the center and wall regions. Explain why physical diffusivity and numerical diffusion require separate experiments.

segments.title: A conservation check
segments.caption: Explain why agreement of the two curves verifies the discrete budget but does not establish physical validity.

segments.title: Reaction and recovery
segments.caption: Identify the depolarizing and outward terms. State what happens to h above and below the gate threshold.

segments.title: Localized stimulation
segments.caption: Locate the stimulus in space and time. Explain why a local source can change voltage elsewhere when D is positive.

segments.title: An advancing front
segments.caption: Compare voltage and availability behind the front. Do not infer a complete recovery time from this window.

segments.title: Propagation through the strand
segments.caption: Keep the physical sensor positions fixed. Predict which threshold crossing occurs first.

segments.title: Conduction-speed measurement
segments.caption: Compute 6 mm divided by the arrival-time difference. Convert mm/ms to m/s and discuss timing error.

segments.title: Corresponding landmarks
segments.caption: Distinguish the physical point set from its labels. Decide which transformations should be removed before comparing shapes.

segments.title: Coordinate interpolation
segments.caption: At t=1/2 calculate the image of every point. Explain why the map is not injective.

segments.title: The endpoint does not certify the path
segments.caption: Compare the final half-turn with the singular midpoint. Checking only the endpoint determinant misses the collapse.

segments.title: Rotation as an ambient flow
segments.caption: Track a point and a nearby grid cell through the first half of the rotation. Show that the determinant stays one.

segments.title: A common endpoint, a different path
segments.caption: Both paths end at a half-turn, but only the rotation remains invertible at every intermediate time.

segments.title: The Jacobian evolution
segments.caption: Core: evaluate the determinant for rotation and explain why finitely sampled numerical determinants are only diagnostics. Optional: derive the determinant formula from the matrix variational equation.
